在贝内特湖造船
迈尔斯峡谷急流（怀特霍斯）
道森城

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Klondike Gold Rush
Parks Canada: Dawson Historical Complex and Chilkoot Trail National Historic Sites
Pierre Berton, Klondike: The Last Great Gold Rush, 1896–1899 (rev. ed., 1972)

note: Keish (Skookum Jim Mason) and Káa Goox (Dawson Charlie) were Tagish men; credit for the discovery was long given to Carmack alone.

story.en:
The discovery was made by a Tagish man, Keish, known as Skookum Jim Mason, with his nephew Káa Goox and his brother-in-law George Carmack, though Carmack registered the claim and was long given the credit. News reached the outside world only in July 1897, when the steamer Portland docked in Seattle with miners carrying gold worth about a million dollars. In a country sunk in depression, thousands quit their jobs.

Canada's North-West Mounted Police required each stampeder entering the Yukon to bring a year's supplies, about a tonne, which meant dozens of trips up the "Golden Stairs" cut in the ice of the Chilkoot Pass. In the spring of 1898 some 7,000 home-made boats set off from Lake Bennett down the Yukon River.

By the time most arrived, the rich creeks had long been staked. Dawson, with perhaps 30,000 people, had opera houses and saloons, but few newcomers found gold, and in 1899 many rushed on to Nome in Alaska. The rush displaced the Hän people of Tr'ochëk, and it inspired Jack London and Robert Service.
story.zh:
发现黄金的是塔吉什人基什（人称斯库库姆·吉姆·梅森），同行的还有他的外甥卡古和他的妹夫乔治·卡马克；不过登记矿权的是卡马克，功劳也长期被记在他一人名下。直到1897年7月，“波特兰”号汽船载着带回约值百万美元黄金的矿工停靠西雅图，消息才传遍外界。在经济萧条中的美国，成千上万人辞掉了工作。

加拿大西北骑警要求每个进入育空的淘金者带够一年的物资，约一吨重，这意味着要沿奇尔库特山口冰面上凿出的“黄金阶梯”往返数十趟。1898年春，约七千条自制小船从贝内特湖出发，顺育空河而下。

等大多数人赶到时，富矿溪流早已被圈占一空。道森城人口或达三万，有歌剧院和酒馆，但新来者很少淘到金子；1899年，许多人又涌向阿拉斯加的诺姆。淘金热迫使特罗切克的汉族原住民迁离家园，也激发了杰克·伦敦和罗伯特·瑟维斯的创作。

name.zh: 莱特兄弟首次动力飞行

summary.en: At Kill Devil Hills near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright flew the Wright Flyer for 12 seconds and 37 metres, the first controlled, sustained flight of a powered, heavier-than-air aircraft. Wilbur flew 260 metres in the fourth flight that day.
summary.zh: 在北卡罗来纳州基蒂霍克附近的斩魔山，奥维尔·莱特驾驶“飞行者一号”飞行了12秒、37米，这是人类首次可控、持续的有动力重于空气的飞行器飞行。当天第四次飞行中，威尔伯飞了260米。

sources.title: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum: The 1903 Wright Flyer
Britannica: Wright brothers
Tom D. Crouch, The Bishop's Boys: A Life of Wilbur and Orville Wright (1989)

story.en:
Wilbur and Orville Wright ran a bicycle shop in Dayton, Ohio, and had no university training. What set them apart was their method. They saw that the real problem of flight was control, not lift or power, and solved it by twisting, or "warping", the wing tips, an idea Wilbur had while fiddling with a long cardboard box. When their gliders performed worse than published tables predicted, they built a small wind tunnel in 1901 and tested some 200 wing shapes.

They chose the Outer Banks for its steady winds, soft sand and privacy. For the 1903 machine they built their own lightweight engine with their mechanic, Charlie Taylor, and designed propellers as rotating wings.

On the cold, windy morning of 17 December, after a failed attempt three days earlier, Orville took off from a wooden rail while a lifesaving station crewman, John Daniels, snapped the famous photograph. Four flights were made before a gust wrecked the plane. Few newspapers believed the story; only after public flights in France in 1908 did the world accept it.
story.zh:
威尔伯·莱特和奥维尔·莱特在俄亥俄州代顿经营一家自行车店，从未受过大学教育。他们与众不同之处在于方法。他们认识到飞行的真正难题是操控，而非升力或动力，并通过扭转翼尖（“翘曲”机翼）解决了这一问题——这个想法是威尔伯摆弄一个长纸盒时想到的。当他们的滑翔机表现不如已发表的数据表预测时，他们于1901年自制了一个小风洞，测试了约200种机翼形状。

他们选中外滩群岛，是看中那里稳定的风、松软的沙地和不受打扰的环境。为1903年的飞机，他们与机械师查理·泰勒一起自制了一台轻型发动机，并把螺旋桨当作旋转的机翼来设计。

12月17日清晨寒风凛冽，在三天前一次失败的尝试之后，奥维尔从一条木轨上起飞，救生站队员约翰·丹尼尔斯按下快门，拍下了那张著名的照片。他们飞了四次，之后一阵狂风毁坏了飞机。几乎没有报纸相信这件事；直到1908年他们在法国公开飞行，世界才接受了这一事实。

summary.en: A magnitude ~7.9 earthquake on the San Andreas Fault struck at 5:12 a.m. on 18 April 1906. The shaking and three days of fires destroyed some 28,000 buildings and about 80 percent of San Francisco and killed an estimated 3,000 people. Its study founded modern earthquake science.
summary.zh: 1906年4月18日清晨5时12分，圣安德烈亚斯断层发生约7.9级地震。地震及随后三天的大火摧毁了约2.8万栋建筑、旧金山约80%的城区，估计约3000人遇难。对这次地震的研究奠定了现代地震科学的基础。

sources.title: USGS: The Great 1906 San Francisco Earthquake
Britannica: San Francisco earthquake of 1906
Simon Winchester, A Crack in the Edge of the World (2005)

note: Official counts at the time listed under 500 dead; later research by Gladys Hansen raised the estimate to about 3,000.

story.en:
The rupture tore along about 470 kilometres of the San Andreas Fault, shifting the ground up to six metres sideways. In San Francisco, built largely on wood and on filled marshland, chimneys collapsed and gas mains broke. Worse, the shaking smashed the water mains and fatally injured the fire chief, Dennis Sullivan.

Fires burned for three days. Soldiers under General Frederick Funston dynamited buildings to create firebreaks, often with the wrong explosives, starting new fires. Mayor Eugene Schmitz ordered looters shot on sight. Half the city's population, about 250,000 people, were left homeless and lived in tents and wooden relief "cottages" in the parks. In Chinatown, officials tried to use the disaster to move Chinese residents out of the city centre; the community resisted and rebuilt.

The destruction of city birth records had an unexpected consequence: Chinese immigrants could claim citizenship by birth and bring over "paper sons". The state commission led by Andrew Lawson produced the first detailed study of fault movement, and H. F. Reid's elastic-rebound theory, drawn from it, still explains how earthquakes work.
story.zh:
断层破裂沿圣安德烈亚斯断层延伸约470公里，地面横向错动达六米。旧金山的建筑大多是木结构，又多建在填平的沼泽地上，烟囱倒塌，煤气管道断裂。更糟的是，地震震断了供水干管，还使消防局长丹尼斯·沙利文受了致命伤。

大火烧了三天。弗雷德里克·芬斯顿将军指挥士兵炸毁建筑以开辟隔火带，却常常用错炸药，反而引发新的火灾。市长尤金·施密茨下令对抢劫者格杀勿论。全城一半人口约25万人无家可归，住进公园里的帐篷和木制救济小屋。在唐人街，官员企图借灾把华人迁出市中心；华人社区奋起抗争，并在原地重建。

城市出生记录被毁带来了意想不到的后果：华人移民可以声称在本地出生而获得公民身份，并据此把“纸上儿子”接来美国。安德鲁·劳森领导的州委员会完成了第一份详尽的断层运动研究，H·F·里德据此提出的弹性回跳理论至今仍是解释地震机制的基础。

name.en: Ford Model T and the moving assembly line
name.zh: 福特T型车与流水装配线

summary.en: Henry Ford's Model T, introduced in 1908, became the first car for ordinary buyers. In 1913 his Highland Park plant near Detroit introduced a moving assembly line that cut the time to build a chassis from about 12 hours to 93 minutes; more than 15 million Model Ts were sold by 1927.
summary.zh: 亨利·福特于1908年推出的T型车成为第一款面向普通消费者的汽车。1913年，他在底特律附近的高地公园工厂引入移动装配线，把组装一台底盘的时间从约12小时缩短到93分钟；到1927年，T型车售出超过1500万辆。

sources.title: The Henry Ford Museum: The Moving Assembly Line
Britannica: Model T
David A. Hounshell, From the American System to Mass Production, 1800–1932 (1984)

note: The Model T was launched in 1908; the record is dated to the introduction of the moving line in 1913.

story.en:
Ford's engineers borrowed the idea from Chicago meatpacking plants, where carcasses moved past workers on overhead trolleys, and reversed it: parts and chassis moved, and each worker stayed at one station doing one task. Experiments began with magneto assembly in April 1913; by the end of the year the whole chassis rode along a line pulled by a rope and then a chain.

The price of a Model T fell from 850 dollars in 1908 to under 300 by the mid-1920s. The work, however, was so monotonous that turnover in 1913 reached about 370 percent. In January 1914 Ford answered with the "five-dollar day", roughly double the going wage, for workers who met the standards of his Sociological Department, whose inspectors visited their homes.

The term "Fordism" came to stand for mass production paired with mass consumption, studied by industrialists from Germany to the Soviet Union. Detroit became the motor city, drawing workers from the American South, Europe and the Middle East.
story.zh:
福特的工程师从芝加哥肉类加工厂借鉴了这一思路：在那里，屠体挂在高架吊车上从工人面前经过。他们把它倒过来用：零件和底盘移动，每个工人固定在一个工位上只做一道工序。1913年4月首先在磁电机装配上试验；到年底，整个底盘都由绳索、后来是链条牵引着沿装配线移动。

T型车的价格从1908年的850美元降到20世纪20年代中期的不足300美元。然而工作单调到1913年的员工流动率高达约370%。1914年1月，福特推出“五美元日薪”作为回应，约为当时工资的两倍，但工人必须符合其“社会部”的标准，该部门的检查员会登门家访。

“福特主义”一词后来代表大规模生产与大众消费的结合，从德国到苏联的实业家都加以研究。底特律成为“汽车城”，吸引了来自美国南方、欧洲和中东的工人。

summary.en: A fire on the upper floors of the Asch Building in Greenwich Village killed 146 garment workers, most of them young Jewish and Italian immigrant women, many of whom jumped from windows because exit doors were locked. Outrage led New York to pass sweeping factory safety and labour laws.
summary.zh: 格林尼治村阿施大楼上层的一场火灾夺去了146名制衣工人的生命，死者大多是犹太裔和意大利裔年轻移民女工；由于安全出口被锁，许多人跳窗身亡。公众的愤怒促使纽约州通过了一系列全面的工厂安全和劳工法律。

sources.title: Cornell University ILR School: Remembering the 1911 Triangle Factory Fire
Britannica: Triangle shirtwaist factory fire
David Von Drehle, Triangle: The Fire That Changed America (2003)

summary.en: Fleeing Jim Crow laws, lynching and sharecropping, about six million African Americans moved from the rural South to cities of the North, Midwest and West. The migration transformed Chicago, Detroit, New York and Los Angeles, American music and politics.
summary.zh: 为逃离吉姆·克劳法、私刑和佃农制度，约六百万非裔美国人从南方农村迁往北部、中西部和西部的城市。这场迁徙改变了芝加哥、底特律、纽约和洛杉矶，也改变了美国的音乐和政治。

sources.title: Britannica: Great Migration
Isabel Wilkerson, The Warmth of Other Suns: The Epic Story of America's Great Migration (2010)
Library of Congress: The African-American Mosaic — The Great Migration

story.en:
When the First World War cut off European immigration, northern factories needed workers. Labour agents and the Chicago Defender, a Black newspaper carried south by Pullman porters, spread news of jobs paying several times what a sharecropper could earn. Families left at night to avoid creditors and sheriffs, boarding the Illinois Central north from Mississippi or the trains from the Carolinas to New York.

The North was not the promised land. Newcomers met restrictive housing covenants, segregated neighbourhoods and violence: in the Chicago race riot of 1919, 38 people were killed. Yet they built new communities. The South Side of Chicago, where Louis Armstrong arrived from New Orleans in 1922, and Harlem became capitals of Black culture, from jazz and blues to the Harlem Renaissance.

A second, larger wave after 1940 went also to the shipyards and factories of California. By 1970 nearly half of all African Americans lived outside the South, and their votes in northern cities helped shape the politics of the New Deal and the civil rights era.
story.zh:
第一次世界大战切断了来自欧洲的移民，北方工厂急需工人。招工代理人以及由普尔曼列车搬运工带到南方的黑人报纸《芝加哥卫报》，传播着工资是佃农收入数倍的工作消息。一家家人趁夜离开，以躲避债主和警长，有的从密西西比搭乘伊利诺伊中央铁路北上，有的从卡罗来纳乘火车前往纽约。

北方并非应许之地。新来者遭遇限制性房产契约、隔离社区和暴力：1919年芝加哥种族骚乱中有38人丧生。但他们建立起新的社区。1922年路易斯·阿姆斯特朗从新奥尔良来到的芝加哥南区，以及纽约的哈莱姆，都成了黑人文化的中心，从爵士乐、布鲁斯到哈莱姆文艺复兴。

1940年后规模更大的第二波迁徙还涌向了加利福尼亚的造船厂和工厂。到1970年，近一半非裔美国人生活在南方以外，他们在北方城市的选票帮助塑造了新政和民权时代的政治。

summary.en: On 6 December 1917 the French munitions ship Mont-Blanc, carrying nearly 3,000 tonnes of explosives, collided with the Norwegian ship Imo in Halifax harbour and blew up in the largest human-made explosion before the atomic bomb. About 2,000 people died and 9,000 were injured.
summary.zh: 1917年12月6日，满载近3000吨炸药的法国军火船“勃朗峰”号在哈利法克斯港与挪威船“伊莫”号相撞后爆炸，这是原子弹问世前人类制造的最大爆炸。约2000人死亡，9000人受伤。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Halifax Explosion
Nova Scotia Archives: Halifax Explosion virtual exhibit
Maritime Museum of the Atlantic: Halifax Explosion

story.en:
Halifax was the main North American port for convoys to wartime Europe, and its harbour narrows were busy. Shortly before nine on a clear morning, the Mont-Blanc, loaded with TNT, picric acid, guncotton and drums of benzol, met the outbound Imo in the Narrows. After a confusion of whistle signals, the Imo struck the French ship's bow. Sparks ignited the benzol, and the crew, knowing what was below, abandoned ship and rowed to the Dartmouth shore.

The burning ship drifted against Pier 6, drawing crowds to windows and the waterfront to watch. Vince Coleman, a railway dispatcher, stayed at his post to telegraph a warning that stopped an incoming passenger train, and was killed. At 9:04 the Mont-Blanc exploded. The blast flattened the Richmond district, a tsunami swept the shore, and the Mi'kmaq community at Turtle Grove was destroyed. Hundreds were blinded by flying glass.

A blizzard followed the next day. Relief trains came from Boston, and Nova Scotia still sends a Christmas tree to Boston each year in thanks.
story.zh:
哈利法克斯是北美向战时欧洲发出船队的主要港口，港内狭窄水道十分繁忙。一个晴朗的早晨，将近九点，满载梯恩梯、苦味酸、火棉和苯桶的“勃朗峰”号在海峡中与出港的“伊莫”号相遇。双方汽笛信号混乱，“伊莫”号撞上了法国船的船首。火星点燃了苯，深知船上装着什么的船员弃船而逃，划向达特茅斯岸边。

燃烧的船漂到6号码头旁，引得人们聚到窗前和海滨观看。铁路调度员文斯·科尔曼坚守岗位，发电报示警，拦下了一列即将进站的客车，自己却遇难身亡。9点04分，“勃朗峰”号爆炸。冲击波夷平了里士满区，海啸席卷海岸，龟林的米克马克人社区被毁。数百人被飞溅的玻璃刺瞎。

第二天又遭暴风雪袭击。救援列车从波士顿赶来，新斯科舍至今每年都向波士顿赠送一棵圣诞树以表谢意。

name.zh: 第十九条修正案：妇女选举权

summary.en: After seven decades of campaigning, the Nineteenth Amendment barred the denial of the vote on account of sex. Tennessee's ratification on 18 August 1920, by a single vote in its House, made it law. Many women of colour remained excluded by state laws for decades.
summary.zh: 经过七十年的抗争，第十九条修正案规定不得因性别剥夺选举权。1920年8月18日，田纳西州众议院以一票之差批准，使修正案生效。但许多有色人种女性在此后数十年间仍被各州法律排斥在投票之外。

sources.title: National Archives (US): 19th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution: Women's Right to Vote (1920)
Britannica: Nineteenth Amendment
Elaine Weiss, The Woman's Hour: The Great Fight to Win the Vote (2018)

note: Pinned at the Tennessee State Capitol in Nashville, where the decisive ratification vote took place; Canada granted most women the federal vote in 1918.

story.en:
The amendment's text had been written by Susan B. Anthony and Elizabeth Cady Stanton in the 1870s and was often called the Anthony Amendment; both died long before it passed. In the 1910s a younger generation pushed harder. Alice Paul's National Woman's Party picketed the White House during the war, and jailed suffragists who went on hunger strike were force-fed. Carrie Chapman Catt's larger association lobbied state by state, and women's war work weakened the old objections.

Congress passed the amendment in June 1919. By August 1920, 35 states had ratified and one more was needed. In Nashville the anti-suffrage "Antis" wore red roses and supporters yellow ones. The deciding vote came from the youngest member of the Tennessee House, 24-year-old Harry Burn, who had worn a red rose but changed his vote after receiving a letter from his mother urging him to be a good boy and help Mrs. Catt.

Some 8 million women voted that November. Many Black women in the South, Native American women and Asian immigrant women would not gain the vote in practice until the 1940s–1960s.
story.zh:
这条修正案的文本是苏珊·B·安东尼和伊丽莎白·卡迪·斯坦顿在19世纪70年代起草的，常被称为“安东尼修正案”；两人在它通过之前很久就已去世。20世纪10年代，年轻一代的斗争更加激烈。爱丽丝·保罗领导的全国妇女党在战时到白宫前示威，入狱的妇女参政论者以绝食抗议，遭到强行灌食。凯丽·查普曼·卡特领导的规模更大的协会则逐州游说，而妇女在战时的工作也削弱了旧有的反对理由。

国会于1919年6月通过修正案。到1920年8月，已有35个州批准，还差一个州。在纳什维尔，反对者佩戴红玫瑰，支持者佩戴黄玫瑰。决定性的一票来自田纳西州众议院最年轻的议员、24岁的哈里·伯恩：他原本佩戴红玫瑰，却在收到母亲的来信后改变了投票，母亲在信中嘱咐他做个好孩子，帮帮卡特夫人。

当年11月，约八百万女性参加了投票。但南方的许多黑人女性、美洲原住民女性和亚裔移民女性，直到20世纪40至60年代才真正获得投票权。

summary.en: In the 1920s and early 1930s Harlem in New York became the centre of a flowering of African American literature, art, music and thought: writers such as Langston Hughes, Zora Neale Hurston and Claude McKay, the scholar Alain Locke's "New Negro", and the jazz of Duke Ellington at the Cotton Club.
summary.zh: 20世纪20年代至30年代初，纽约哈莱姆成为非裔美国人文学、艺术、音乐和思想繁荣的中心：兰斯顿·休斯、佐拉·尼尔·赫斯顿、克劳德·麦凯等作家，学者阿兰·洛克提出的“新黑人”，以及棉花俱乐部里艾灵顿公爵的爵士乐。

sources.title: Britannica: Harlem Renaissance
Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, New York Public Library
David Levering Lewis, When Harlem Was in Vogue (1981)

note: The movement has no fixed dates; c. 1918–1937 is often given.

summary.en: Five Alberta women, the "Famous Five" led by Emily Murphy, asked whether women were "persons" eligible to sit in Canada's Senate. The Supreme Court of Canada said no, but on appeal the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London ruled in 1929 that they were, calling the constitution a "living tree".
summary.zh: 以埃米莉·墨菲为首的五位艾伯塔女性——“著名五人”——就女性是否属于有资格出任加拿大参议员的“人”提出质询。加拿大最高法院给出否定答案，但伦敦枢密院司法委员会于1929年在上诉中裁定女性属于“人”，并称宪法是一棵“活的树”。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Persons Case
Edwards v. Canada (Attorney General), [1930] AC 124 (Privy Council)
Library and Archives Canada: The Persons Case

name.en: Wall Street Crash and the Great Depression

summary.en: After a speculative boom, the New York Stock Exchange collapsed in late October 1929, culminating in Black Tuesday on 29 October. Bank failures, falling prices and collapsing trade followed; by 1933 about a quarter of US workers and nearly 30 percent of Canadian workers were unemployed.
summary.zh: 经过一轮投机热潮，纽约证券交易所于1929年10月下旬崩盘，在10月29日“黑色星期二”达到顶点。随后银行倒闭、物价下跌、贸易崩溃；到1933年，美国约四分之一的劳动者和加拿大近30%的劳动者失业。

sources.title: Britannica: Stock market crash of 1929
John Kenneth Galbraith, The Great Crash 1929 (1955)
The Canadian Encyclopedia: Great Depression

story.en:
Through the 1920s ordinary Americans had bought stocks on margin, borrowing up to ninety percent of the price, and the market had nearly quadrupled since 1924. In early September 1929 it peaked. On Thursday 24 October panic selling began, and a pool of bankers meeting at J. P. Morgan's offices briefly steadied prices. The following Tuesday 16 million shares changed hands, a record that stood for decades, and ticker tape ran hours behind.

The crash alone did not cause the Depression, but it destroyed confidence and wealth just as the economy was weakening. Thousands of banks failed between 1930 and 1933, wiping out savings; the Smoot–Hawley tariff of 1930 and retaliation by other countries helped cut world trade by about two thirds.

Shanty towns called Hoovervilles grew in city parks. In Canada, whose economy depended on exports of wheat and lumber, prairie farm incomes collapsed and unemployed men rode freight trains west; their On-to-Ottawa Trek ended in a riot in Regina in 1935. Recovery came only with the Second World War.
story.zh:
整个20世纪20年代，普通美国人用保证金购买股票，最多可借入股价的九成，股市自1924年以来涨了近三倍。1929年9月初股市见顶。10月24日星期四，恐慌性抛售开始，一批银行家在J·P·摩根的办公室聚会，一度稳住了股价。随后的星期二，成交量达到1600万股，这一纪录保持了数十年，股票行情收报机滞后了好几个小时。

股灾本身并未造成大萧条，但它在经济正走弱之时摧毁了信心和财富。1930至1933年间，数千家银行倒闭，储蓄化为乌有；1930年的《斯穆特—霍利关税法》及他国的报复措施使世界贸易萎缩了约三分之二。

被称为“胡佛村”的棚户区出现在城市公园里。加拿大经济依赖小麦和木材出口，草原农场收入一落千丈，失业男子扒火车向西流浪；1935年他们发起的“向渥太华进军”在里贾纳以骚乱告终。直到第二次世界大战，经济才真正复苏。

summary.en: Severe drought on the southern Great Plains, where deep ploughing had stripped the native grass, produced enormous dust storms that stripped topsoil from millions of hectares. Hundreds of thousands of farm families left, many for California, and the crisis led to federal soil conservation.
summary.zh: 大平原南部此前因深耕而失去原生草被，严重干旱引发巨大的沙尘暴，数百万公顷土地的表土被刮走。数十万农户背井离乡，许多人去了加利福尼亚；这场危机促成了联邦水土保持政策。

sources.title: Britannica: Dust Bowl
Donald Worster, Dust Bowl: The Southern Plains in the 1930s (1979)
National Drought Mitigation Center, University of Nebraska: The Dust Bowl

note: Drought years on the Plains are variously dated 1930–1936 or 1931–1939.

story.en:
During and after the First World War, high wheat prices and new tractors encouraged farmers to plough up tens of millions of acres of the shortgrass prairie of Oklahoma, Texas, Kansas, Colorado and New Mexico, whose deep-rooted grasses had held the soil for thousands of years. When drought struck in the early 1930s, the bare earth simply blew away.

On Black Sunday, 14 April 1935, a wall of dust hundreds of kilometres long rolled across the Panhandle, turning day into night; a reporter's dispatch about it gave the region its name. Children died of "dust pneumonia", and dust from the Plains settled on ships in the Atlantic and on the Capitol in Washington while the soil scientist Hugh Bennett was testifying to Congress.

The new Soil Conservation Service paid farmers to plant shelterbelts, contour-plough and let fields return to grass. Some 200,000 or more migrants from Oklahoma and neighbouring states, called "Okies", drove west on Route 66, a journey made famous by John Steinbeck's novel The Grapes of Wrath and by Dorothea Lange's photographs.
story.zh:
第一次世界大战期间及战后，高企的小麦价格和新式拖拉机促使农民在俄克拉何马、得克萨斯、堪萨斯、科罗拉多和新墨西哥开垦了数千万英亩短草草原，而那些根系深长的草数千年来一直固定着土壤。20世纪30年代初干旱来袭，裸露的土地被风直接卷走。

1935年4月14日“黑色星期日”，一道长达数百公里的沙尘墙席卷狭长地带，白昼顿成黑夜；一位记者有关此事的报道使这一地区得名“尘碗”。孩子们死于“尘埃肺炎”；平原的尘土落到大西洋的船只上，也落到华盛顿的国会大厦上——当时土壤学家休·贝内特正在国会作证。

新成立的水土保持局出钱让农民种植防护林带、等高耕作，并让农田重新长草。二十万以上来自俄克拉何马及邻近各州的移民（被称为“俄克佬”）沿66号公路西行，约翰·斯坦贝克的小说《愤怒的葡萄》和多萝西娅·兰格的照片使这段旅程举世闻名。

summary.en: Franklin D. Roosevelt's programmes of relief, recovery and reform, launched in his first hundred days in 1933, insured bank deposits, regulated stock markets, employed millions in public works such as the Civilian Conservation Corps and the Tennessee Valley Authority, and created Social Security in 1935.
summary.zh: 富兰克林·D·罗斯福在1933年就职后的“百日新政”中推出救济、复兴和改革计划：为银行存款提供保险、监管证券市场、通过民间资源保护队和田纳西河谷管理局等公共工程雇用数百万人，并于1935年建立社会保障制度。

sources.title: Britannica: New Deal
Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library and Museum: The New Deal
David M. Kennedy, Freedom from Fear: The American People in Depression and War, 1929–1945 (1999)

story.en:
Roosevelt took office on 4 March 1933 with the banking system collapsing; his inaugural address told the country that the only thing it had to fear was fear itself. He closed every bank for a "holiday", and within a week Congress passed an emergency banking act. On 12 March he explained it to some 60 million listeners in the first of his radio "fireside chats", and when the banks reopened, deposits exceeded withdrawals.

In the following hundred days Congress passed fifteen major laws. The Civilian Conservation Corps sent young men to plant some three billion trees; the Tennessee Valley Authority built dams that brought electricity to one of the poorest regions in the country. Later programmes, the Works Progress Administration and the Social Security Act of 1935, employed writers and artists as well as labourers and created old-age pensions and unemployment insurance.

The New Deal did not end the Depression, and many programmes excluded farm and domestic workers, a choice that left out most Black Southerners. But it permanently enlarged the federal government's role, and the coalition it built dominated US politics for a generation.
story.zh:
1933年3月4日罗斯福就职时，银行体系正在崩溃；他在就职演说中告诉全国，唯一值得恐惧的是恐惧本身。他下令所有银行“放假”，一周之内国会就通过了紧急银行法。3月12日，他通过第一次广播“炉边谈话”向约六千万听众解释这一措施；银行重新开门时，存款超过了取款。

在随后的一百天里，国会通过了十五项重要法律。民间资源保护队派年轻人植树约三十亿株；田纳西河谷管理局修建水坝，把电力送到全国最贫困的地区之一。后来的公共事业振兴署和1935年《社会保障法》，既雇用劳工也雇用作家和艺术家，并建立了养老金和失业保险制度。

新政并没有终结大萧条，许多项目把农业工人和家政工人排除在外，使南方的大多数黑人被拒之门外。但它永久性地扩大了联邦政府的职能，它所建立的政治联盟主导美国政治长达一代人之久。

name.zh: 日裔美国人被集中关押

summary.en: After Pearl Harbor, Executive Order 9066 (February 1942) led to the forced removal of about 120,000 people of Japanese descent, two thirds of them US citizens, from the West Coast to ten inland camps. Canada likewise removed some 22,000 Japanese Canadians from coastal British Columbia. Both governments later apologised and paid redress (1988).
summary.zh: 珍珠港事件后，1942年2月的第9066号行政命令导致约十二万日裔居民（其中三分之二是美国公民）被强制迁离西海岸，关进内陆的十座营地。加拿大也把约两万两千名日裔加拿大人迁离不列颠哥伦比亚沿海地区。两国政府后来均道歉并支付了赔偿（1988年）。

sources.title: National Archives (US): Executive Order 9066
National Park Service: Manzanar National Historic Site
The Canadian Encyclopedia: Internment of Japanese Canadians

note: Pinned at Manzanar, California, one of the ten War Relocation Authority camps.

story.en:
No act of espionage or sabotage by a Japanese American was ever proven, yet in the weeks after Pearl Harbor politicians, newspapers and the army's western commander, General John DeWitt, demanded mass removal. Families were given days to sell homes, farms and businesses, often for a fraction of their value, and could take only what they could carry.

They were held first in "assembly centres" at racetracks, sleeping in horse stalls, then sent to barbed-wire camps in deserts and swamps such as Manzanar in California and Heart Mountain in Wyoming. Even so, some 33,000 Japanese Americans served in the military; the 442nd Regimental Combat Team, made up largely of Nisei, became one of the most decorated units of the war.

Fred Korematsu refused to report and was convicted; the Supreme Court upheld his conviction in 1944. Decades later a federal commission concluded that the removal had been driven by race prejudice, war hysteria and a failure of political leadership. In 1988 President Reagan signed the Civil Liberties Act, apologising and paying 20,000 dollars to each survivor; Canada announced its own redress the same year.
story.zh:
从未有任何日裔美国人被证实从事过间谍或破坏活动，但珍珠港事件后的几周里，政客、报纸和陆军西部司令约翰·德威特将军都要求大规模迁移。一家家人只有几天时间变卖房屋、农场和店铺，往往只得到其价值的零头，而且只能携带随身行李。

他们先被关押在赛马场改成的“集合中心”，睡在马厩里，然后被送往沙漠和沼泽中的铁丝网营地，如加利福尼亚的曼扎纳和怀俄明的心山。即便如此，仍有约三万三千名日裔美国人在军中服役；主要由第二代日裔组成的第442团级战斗队成为战争中获勋最多的部队之一。

是松丰三郎（弗雷德·是松）拒绝报到而被定罪，最高法院于1944年维持原判。数十年后，一个联邦委员会认定，这场迁移是种族偏见、战争歇斯底里和政治领导失职的产物。1988年，里根总统签署《公民自由法》，正式道歉并向每位幸存者赔偿两万美元；加拿大也在同年宣布了赔偿方案。

summary.en: Fearing a German atomic bomb, the United States, with Britain and Canada, built a secret network of laboratories and plants employing some 130,000 people. Under General Leslie Groves and the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer it produced the first nuclear weapons, tested at Trinity and used against Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945.
summary.zh: 由于担心德国研制原子弹，美国联合英国和加拿大建立了一个秘密的实验室和工厂网络，雇用约13万人。在莱斯利·格罗夫斯将军和物理学家J·罗伯特·奥本海默领导下，它制造出最早的核武器，先在“三位一体”试验中试爆，1945年8月又投向广岛和长崎。

label.zh: 芝加哥一号堆：首次链式反应
橡树岭：铀浓缩
汉福德：钚生产堆
洛斯阿拉莫斯：原子弹设计实验室

label.en: Chalk River, Ontario: Anglo-Canadian reactor project
label.zh: 安大略乔克河：英加反应堆项目
新墨西哥“三位一体”试验

sources.title: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of History: The Manhattan Project: An Interactive History
Britannica: Manhattan Project
Richard Rhodes, The Making of the Atomic Bomb (1986)

story.en:
In August 1939 Albert Einstein signed a letter, drafted by Leo Szilard, warning President Roosevelt that Germany might build "extremely powerful bombs" from uranium. Little happened until 1942, when the army took over and put the forceful engineer Leslie Groves in charge. He chose Oppenheimer, a brilliant but unlikely Berkeley theorist, to lead a new weapons laboratory on a remote mesa at Los Alamos, New Mexico.

On 2 December 1942 Enrico Fermi's team achieved the first controlled nuclear chain reaction in a pile of graphite and uranium under the stands of a University of Chicago football field. Then came industry on a vast scale: at Oak Ridge, Tennessee, plants separated fissile uranium-235; at Hanford, Washington, reactors on the Columbia River made plutonium. Most of the workers had no idea what they were building.

The project cost about two billion dollars. Its scientists debated whether the bomb should be demonstrated before use; a committee chaired by James Franck and a petition organised by Szilard urged against a surprise attack on Japan. After Hiroshima and Nagasaki, many, Oppenheimer among them, spent years arguing for international control of atomic energy.
story.zh:
1939年8月，阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦签署了一封由利奥·西拉德起草的信，提醒罗斯福总统德国可能用铀制造出威力极大的炸弹。此后进展甚微，直到1942年陆军接管，由作风强势的工程师莱斯利·格罗夫斯负责。他选中了才华出众却看似不合适的伯克利理论物理学家奥本海默，在新墨西哥州偏远的洛斯阿拉莫斯台地上领导一座新的武器实验室。

1942年12月2日，恩里科·费米的团队在芝加哥大学一座橄榄球场看台下用石墨和铀堆成的反应堆中，实现了第一次受控核链式反应。随之而来的是规模空前的工业工程：田纳西州橡树岭的工厂分离出可裂变的铀-235，华盛顿州哥伦比亚河畔汉福德的反应堆生产钚。大多数工人根本不知道自己在造什么。

这个计划耗资约二十亿美元。科学家们曾争论是否应在使用前先公开演示；詹姆斯·弗兰克主持的委员会和西拉德组织的请愿书都反对对日本发动突然袭击。广岛和长崎之后，包括奥本海默在内的许多人用多年时间呼吁对原子能实行国际管制。

summary.en: At 5:29 a.m. on 16 July 1945, on the Alamogordo Bombing Range in the New Mexico desert, Manhattan Project scientists detonated a plutonium implosion device with a yield of about 21 kilotons, opening the nuclear age. Fallout spread over nearby communities, whose residents were not warned.
summary.zh: 1945年7月16日清晨5时29分，曼哈顿计划的科学家在新墨西哥沙漠的阿拉莫戈多轰炸靶场引爆了一枚钚内爆装置，当量约2.1万吨，开启了核时代。放射性沉降物飘落到附近社区，当地居民事先并未得到警告。

sources.title: U.S. Department of Energy: Trinity Site — World's First Nuclear Explosion
White Sands Missile Range: Trinity Site
Kai Bird & Martin J. Sherwin, American Prometheus: The Triumph and Tragedy of J. Robert Oppenheimer (2005)

story.en:
The uranium bomb design was so simple that no test was thought necessary, but the plutonium bomb depended on squeezing a metal core with a perfectly symmetrical shell of explosives, and no one was sure it would work. Oppenheimer named the test site Trinity, perhaps after a sonnet by John Donne. The device, nicknamed the Gadget, was hoisted to the top of a 30-metre steel tower.

Thunderstorms delayed the shot until just before dawn. Observers lay face-down in trenches ten kilometres away, some watching through welding glass. The flash lit the mountains brighter than noon, the fireball rose into a mushroom cloud twelve kilometres high, and the heat melted the desert sand into a green glass later called trinitite. Fermi dropped scraps of paper to estimate the yield from how far the blast wave carried them.

Oppenheimer later said a line from the Bhagavad Gita came to his mind, about becoming death, the destroyer of worlds. The army's cover story spoke of an ammunition dump explosion. Three weeks later the first atomic bomb fell on Hiroshima.
story.zh:
铀弹的设计非常简单，被认为无需试验；而钚弹则要靠一层完全对称的炸药外壳挤压金属核心，谁也没有把握它能成功。奥本海默把试验场命名为“三位一体”，可能取自约翰·多恩的一首十四行诗。这个绰号“小玩意”的装置被吊上一座30米高的钢塔顶端。

雷暴使试验推迟到黎明前夕。观测者趴在十公里外的壕沟里，有人透过焊接护目镜观看。闪光把群山照得比正午还亮，火球升起，化作十二公里高的蘑菇云，高温把沙漠的沙子熔成一种绿色玻璃，后来被称为“三位一体石”。费米撒下几片碎纸，根据冲击波把它们吹出多远来估算当量。

奥本海默后来说，当时他想起了《薄伽梵歌》中的一句话：我成了死神，世界的毁灭者。军方对外谎称是弹药库爆炸。三周后，第一颗原子弹落在了广岛。

name.zh: 布朗诉托皮卡教育局案

summary.en: In a unanimous ruling written by Chief Justice Earl Warren, the US Supreme Court held that state-mandated racial segregation in public schools violated the Fourteenth Amendment, overturning the "separate but equal" doctrine of Plessy v. Ferguson (1896). Southern states resisted desegregation for years.
summary.zh: 美国最高法院在首席大法官厄尔·沃伦执笔的一致判决中裁定，各州强制实行的公立学校种族隔离违反第十四条修正案，推翻了1896年“普莱西诉弗格森案”确立的“隔离但平等”原则。南方各州此后多年抵制取消隔离。

sources.title: National Park Service: Brown v. Board of Education National Historical Park
Britannica: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
Richard Kluger, Simple Justice (1976)

story.en:
Linda Brown, a Black third-grader in Topeka, Kansas, had to cross railway tracks and ride a bus to a segregated school although a white school stood a few blocks from home. In 1951 her father Oliver Brown and other parents, organised by the NAACP, sued the school board. Their case was joined with others from South Carolina, Virginia, Delaware and Washington, D.C.

The NAACP's chief lawyer, Thurgood Marshall, argued that segregation itself was unequal. His team cited the "doll tests" of the psychologists Kenneth and Mamie Clark, in which Black children preferred white dolls, as evidence of the harm done. When Chief Justice Fred Vinson died in 1953, his successor Earl Warren worked to bring every justice to agree, believing a divided court would invite defiance.

The ruling declared that in public education separate facilities are inherently unequal. A second decision in 1955 ordered desegregation only "with all deliberate speed", and Southern officials launched "massive resistance": in 1957 President Eisenhower had to send paratroopers to escort nine Black students into Central High School in Little Rock. Marshall became the first African American Supreme Court justice in 1967.
story.zh:
堪萨斯州托皮卡的黑人三年级学生琳达·布朗，家附近几个街区就有一所白人学校，她却必须穿过铁道、乘公共汽车去上一所种族隔离学校。1951年，在全国有色人种协进会的组织下，她的父亲奥利弗·布朗和其他家长起诉了学区教育委员会。此案与来自南卡罗来纳、弗吉尼亚、特拉华和华盛顿特区的案件合并审理。

协进会首席律师瑟古德·马歇尔主张，隔离本身就是不平等的。他的团队援引心理学家肯尼斯·克拉克和玛米·克拉克的“玩偶测试”——黑人儿童更喜欢白人玩偶——作为隔离造成伤害的证据。1953年首席大法官弗雷德·文森去世后，继任者厄尔·沃伦努力争取每一位大法官的同意，因为他相信分裂的判决会招致抗拒。

判决宣布，在公共教育领域，隔离的设施本质上就是不平等的。1955年的第二次判决只要求“以十分审慎的速度”取消隔离，南方官员随即发起“大规模抵抗”：1957年，艾森豪威尔总统不得不派伞兵护送九名黑人学生进入小石城中央中学。1967年，马歇尔成为美国第一位非裔最高法院大法官。

name.zh: 蒙哥马利公交车抵制运动

summary.en: After Rosa Parks was arrested on 1 December 1955 for refusing to give up her bus seat to a white man, Black residents of Montgomery, Alabama, boycotted the city buses for 381 days, led by the young minister Martin Luther King Jr. A federal court ruling, upheld by the Supreme Court, ended bus segregation.
summary.zh: 1955年12月1日，罗莎·帕克斯因拒绝把公交车座位让给一名白人男子而被捕。此后，阿拉巴马州蒙哥马利的黑人居民在年轻牧师马丁·路德·金的领导下抵制市内公交车381天。联邦法院的判决（获最高法院维持）终结了公交车上的种族隔离。

sources.title: Britannica: Montgomery bus boycott
Stanford University, Martin Luther King, Jr. Research and Education Institute: Montgomery Bus Boycott
Taylor Branch, Parting the Waters: America in the King Years, 1954–63 (1988)

story.en:
Rosa Parks was not simply a tired seamstress, as the legend later put it. She was secretary of the local NAACP chapter and had trained at the Highlander Folk School in organising. When the driver ordered her to stand on 1 December, she refused, and was arrested.

The Women's Political Council, led by the teacher Jo Ann Robinson, had planned a boycott for years. That night Robinson and her students secretly ran off tens of thousands of leaflets on a college mimeograph machine calling for Black riders to stay off the buses on 5 December, the day of Parks's trial. The boycott was so complete that leaders formed the Montgomery Improvement Association to continue it, electing as president the 26-year-old pastor of Dexter Avenue Baptist Church, Martin Luther King Jr.

For more than a year about 40,000 people walked, shared cars and used a car-pool system of some 300 vehicles. King's house was bombed and he and dozens of others were indicted. In Browder v. Gayle a federal court ruled bus segregation unconstitutional; the Supreme Court affirmed, and on 21 December 1956 King rode at the front of an integrated bus.
story.zh:
罗莎·帕克斯并不像后来的传说那样只是一个疲惫的女裁缝。她是全国有色人种协进会当地分会的秘书，还在海兰德民众学校接受过组织工作培训。12月1日司机命令她让座，她拒绝了，随即被捕。

由教师乔·安·罗宾逊领导的妇女政治委员会多年前就筹划过抵制行动。当晚，罗宾逊和她的学生用学院的油印机偷偷印了数万份传单，号召黑人乘客在12月5日——帕克斯受审的那天——不乘公交车。抵制行动响应之彻底，使领导者们成立了“蒙哥马利改进协会”继续这一行动，并推选德克斯特大道浸信会26岁的牧师马丁·路德·金为主席。

一年多的时间里，约四万人步行、拼车，并依靠一套约300辆车组成的拼车系统出行。金的住宅被炸，他和其他数十人遭到起诉。在“布劳德诉盖尔案”中，联邦法院裁定公交车隔离违宪；最高法院维持了这一判决。1956年12月21日，金坐在一辆不再实行隔离的公交车前排。

summary.en: After the death of the conservative premier Maurice Duplessis, Jean Lesage's Liberal government ("Maîtres chez nous") took education and health out of the hands of the Catholic Church, nationalised hydroelectric power and built a modern Québécois state, fuelling a new nationalism.
summary.zh: 保守派省长莫里斯·杜普莱西去世后，让·勒萨热领导的自由党政府（口号“做自己家园的主人”）把教育和医疗从天主教会手中收归省府，将水电国有化，建立起现代魁北克国家机构，并催生了新的民族主义。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Quiet Revolution
Kenneth McRoberts, Quebec: Social Change and Political Crisis (3rd ed., 1993)

note: The term is usually applied to the Lesage years, 1960–1966, though the changes continued afterwards.

name.en: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
name.zh: 为工作和自由向华盛顿进军

summary.en: About 250,000 people gathered at the Lincoln Memorial to demand civil and economic rights for African Americans. Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech closed the day, building pressure that led to the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
summary.zh: 约25万人聚集在林肯纪念堂前，要求保障非裔美国人的公民权利和经济权利。马丁·路德·金的演说《我有一个梦想》为这一天画上句号，由此形成的压力促成了1964年《民权法》和1965年《选举权法》。

sources.title: National Park Service: Lincoln Memorial — The March on Washington
Britannica: March on Washington
William P. Jones, The March on Washington: Jobs, Freedom, and the Forgotten History of Civil Rights (2013)

story.en:
The march was the idea of A. Philip Randolph, the veteran leader of the sleeping-car porters' union, who had threatened a similar march in 1941. Its organiser was Bayard Rustin, a brilliant strategist kept in the background by some leaders because he was gay and had once been a communist. In under two months he arranged buses, trains, first-aid stations and toilets for a quarter of a million people.

That spring, television had shown police in Birmingham, Alabama, turning fire hoses and dogs on children, and President Kennedy had sent a civil rights bill to Congress. The Kennedy administration feared violence; instead the day was peaceful. Marian Anderson and Mahalia Jackson sang, and John Lewis, aged 23, gave a fiery speech that older leaders had toned down.

King spoke last. Partway through his prepared text, Mahalia Jackson called out to him to tell them about the dream, and he set his notes aside for the passages that made the speech famous. Within two years Congress outlawed segregation in public places and protected voting rights. Eighteen days after the march, a bomb at a Birmingham church killed four girls.
story.zh:
进军的设想出自卧铺车厢搬运工工会的老领袖A·菲利普·伦道夫，他在1941年就曾以类似的进军相威胁。组织者是贝亚德·拉斯廷，一位杰出的策略家，但因为他是同性恋者、又曾是共产党人，一些领导人让他留在幕后。他在不到两个月内为二十五万人安排好了大巴、火车、急救站和厕所。

那年春天，电视上播出了阿拉巴马州伯明翰警察用消防水龙和警犬对付儿童的画面，肯尼迪总统已向国会提交民权法案。肯尼迪政府担心发生暴力，结果这一天却平和有序。玛丽安·安德森和玛哈莉亚·杰克逊献唱，23岁的约翰·刘易斯发表了一篇经老一辈领袖修改得温和了些、却依然激昂的演说。

金最后一个发言。讲到预备稿的一半时，玛哈莉亚·杰克逊朝他喊道，跟他们讲讲那个梦想；他便放下讲稿，说出了使这篇演说名垂青史的段落。两年之内，国会宣布公共场所种族隔离为非法，并保障了投票权。进军十八天后，伯明翰一座教堂发生爆炸，四名女孩遇难。

summary.en: President John F. Kennedy was shot and killed while riding in an open motorcade through Dealey Plaza in Dallas, Texas. Lyndon B. Johnson was sworn in aboard Air Force One. The accused gunman, Lee Harvey Oswald, was himself shot dead two days later.
summary.zh: 约翰·F·肯尼迪总统乘敞篷车队经过得克萨斯州达拉斯迪利广场时中弹身亡。林登·B·约翰逊在“空军一号”上宣誓就职。被控行刺的李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德两天后也被枪杀。

sources.title: John F. Kennedy Presidential Library: November 22, 1963 — Death of the President
Report of the President's Commission on the Assassination of President Kennedy (Warren Commission, 1964)
Britannica: Assassination of John F. Kennedy

summary.en: Held for Canada's centennial on islands built and enlarged in the St. Lawrence, Expo 67 drew over 50 million visits and showcased Buckminster Fuller's geodesic dome and Moshe Safdie's Habitat 67. It is remembered as a high point of Canadian confidence.
summary.zh: 为庆祝加拿大建国百年，1967年世博会在圣劳伦斯河中新建和扩建的岛屿上举行，参观人次超过五千万，展出了巴克敏斯特·富勒的网格穹顶和摩西·萨夫迪的“栖息地67”住宅。它被视为加拿大自信的巅峰时刻。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Expo 67
Library and Archives Canada: Expo 67 – Man and His World

summary.en: When police raided the Stonewall Inn, a gay bar in Greenwich Village, in the early hours of 28 June 1969, patrons and neighbours fought back, and protests continued for several nights. The uprising became the catalyst of the modern LGBTQ rights movement; the first Pride marches marked its anniversary in 1970.
summary.zh: 1969年6月28日凌晨，警察突袭格林尼治村的同性恋酒吧石墙酒馆，酒客和街坊奋起反抗，抗议持续了数个夜晚。这次起义成为现代LGBTQ权利运动的催化剂；1970年为纪念一周年举行了最早的“骄傲大游行”。

sources.title: National Park Service: Stonewall National Monument
Britannica: Stonewall riots
David Carter, Stonewall: The Riots That Sparked the Gay Revolution (2004)

summary.en: Launched from Kennedy Space Center on 16 July 1969, Apollo 11 carried Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins to the Moon. On 20 July Armstrong and Aldrin landed the lunar module Eagle in the Sea of Tranquility and became the first humans to walk on another world, watched by some 600 million people on television.
summary.zh: 1969年7月16日，阿波罗11号从肯尼迪航天中心发射，载着尼尔·阿姆斯特朗、巴兹·奥尔德林和迈克尔·柯林斯飞向月球。7月20日，阿姆斯特朗和奥尔德林驾驶登月舱“鹰”号降落在静海，成为最早在另一个天体上行走的人类，全球约六亿人通过电视观看。

sources.title: NASA: Apollo 11 Mission Overview
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum: Apollo 11
Britannica: Apollo 11

note: Pinned at Launch Complex 39A, Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

story.en:
In May 1961, weeks after Yuri Gagarin's orbit and the Bay of Pigs fiasco, President Kennedy asked Congress to commit the United States to landing a man on the Moon before the decade was out. At its peak the Apollo programme employed some 400,000 people, from engineers at Huntsville and Houston to the seamstresses who sewed spacesuits layer by layer. In January 1967 a fire in the Apollo 1 capsule killed three astronauts during a rehearsal, and the spacecraft was redesigned.

On 20 July 1969, as Eagle descended, the guidance computer flashed alarms it was overloaded, and Armstrong saw that the autopilot was taking them towards a field of boulders. He flew the module by hand to a clear spot, landing with roughly half a minute of usable fuel left before an abort would have been called. "The Eagle has landed," he radioed to Houston.

Six and a half hours later he stepped onto the surface. Armstrong and Aldrin spent about two and a half hours outside, planting a flag, setting up experiments and collecting 21.5 kilograms of rock, while Collins orbited alone overhead. They splashed down in the Pacific on 24 July.
story.zh:
1961年5月，就在尤里·加加林绕地球飞行和猪湾事件惨败几周之后，肯尼迪总统要求国会承诺在这个十年结束前把人送上月球。阿波罗计划高峰时雇用约四十万人，从亨茨维尔和休斯敦的工程师，到一层层缝制航天服的女裁缝。1967年1月，阿波罗1号舱在一次演练中起火，三名宇航员遇难，飞船随后被重新设计。

1969年7月20日，“鹰”号下降时，制导计算机不断闪出过载警报，阿姆斯特朗又发现自动驾驶正把他们带向一片巨石区。他手动驾驶登月舱飞到一处平坦地点降落，此时离必须中止着陆的界限只剩约半分钟可用燃料。他向休斯敦报告：“‘鹰’已着陆。”

六个半小时后，他踏上了月面。阿姆斯特朗和奥尔德林在舱外活动了约两个半小时，插上国旗、布设实验装置，采集了21.5公斤岩石，柯林斯则独自在上空绕月飞行。7月24日，他们在太平洋溅落。

name.zh: 阿帕网发出第一条消息

summary.en: On 29 October 1969 a student programmer in Leonard Kleinrock's lab at UCLA sent the first message over the ARPANET, the Pentagon-funded packet-switched network that grew into the Internet, to a computer at the Stanford Research Institute. The system crashed after two letters.
summary.zh: 1969年10月29日，加州大学洛杉矶分校伦纳德·克莱因罗克实验室的一名学生程序员，通过五角大楼资助的分组交换网络阿帕网，向斯坦福研究所的一台计算机发出了第一条消息；这个网络后来发展为互联网。系统在传送两个字母后便崩溃了。

sources.title: UCLA Samueli School of Engineering: The Birth of the Internet (Kleinrock Internet Heritage Site)
Britannica: ARPANET
Katie Hafner & Matthew Lyon, Where Wizards Stay Up Late: The Origins of the Internet (1996)

story.en:
The ARPANET was built by the Defense Department's Advanced Research Projects Agency to let researchers at different universities share scarce, expensive computers. It used an idea developed independently by Paul Baran in the United States and Donald Davies in Britain: break data into small packets that travel separately and are reassembled at the end, so the network has no single point of failure.

The first two nodes were refrigerator-sized Interface Message Processors built by the Cambridge firm Bolt Beranek and Newman. At about 10:30 p.m. on 29 October 1969, UCLA student Charley Kline began typing the command LOGIN to the SRI machine 560 kilometres away, while talking to his counterpart Bill Duvall by telephone. After L and O, the Stanford system crashed. About an hour later the full login went through.

By December the network linked four sites, adding Santa Barbara and Utah. Email arrived in 1971. In 1983 the ARPANET adopted the TCP/IP protocols designed by Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn, the common language of today's Internet.
story.zh:
阿帕网由美国国防部高级研究计划局建造，目的是让不同大学的研究人员共享稀缺而昂贵的计算机。它采用了由美国的保罗·巴兰和英国的唐纳德·戴维斯分别独立提出的思路：把数据拆成小的分组，各自传输，到终点再重新组装，这样网络就没有单一的故障点。

最早的两个节点是剑桥市BBN公司制造的冰箱大小的“接口信息处理机”。1969年10月29日晚上10点半左右，加州大学洛杉矶分校学生查理·克莱恩一边通过电话与对方的比尔·杜瓦尔交谈，一边开始向560公里外斯坦福研究所的计算机输入登录指令LOGIN。输入L和O之后，斯坦福的系统崩溃了。约一小时后，完整的登录才得以完成。

到12月，网络连接了四个站点，加入了圣巴巴拉和犹他。电子邮件于1971年出现。1983年，阿帕网采用了温特·瑟夫和鲍勃·卡恩设计的TCP/IP协议，这就是今天互联网的通用语言。

name.zh: 塞尔玛至蒙哥马利游行

summary.en: On "Bloody Sunday", 7 March 1965, Alabama state troopers beat voting-rights marchers led by John Lewis and Hosea Williams on Selma's Edmund Pettus Bridge. Televised images shocked the nation; a protected march reached Montgomery on 25 March, and Congress passed the Voting Rights Act that August.
summary.zh: 1965年3月7日“血腥星期日”，阿拉巴马州警在塞尔玛的埃德蒙·佩特斯桥上殴打约翰·刘易斯和霍西·威廉斯率领的争取投票权游行者。电视画面震惊全国；3月25日，一支受到保护的游行队伍抵达蒙哥马利，国会于当年8月通过了《选举权法》。

sources.title: National Park Service: Selma to Montgomery National Historic Trail
Britannica: Selma March
Gary May, Bending Toward Justice: The Voting Rights Act and the Transformation of American Democracy (2013)

summary.en: The Front de libération du Québec kidnapped British diplomat James Cross and Québec labour minister Pierre Laporte in October 1970. Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau invoked the War Measures Act, the only peacetime use, and nearly 500 people were detained without charge; Laporte was found murdered.
summary.zh: 1970年10月，魁北克解放阵线绑架了英国外交官詹姆斯·克罗斯和魁北克劳工部长皮埃尔·拉波特。皮埃尔·特鲁多总理援引《战时措施法》，这是该法唯一一次在和平时期使用，近500人未经起诉即遭拘押；拉波特后被发现遇害。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: October Crisis
Library and Archives Canada: The October Crisis
William Tetley, The October Crisis, 1970: An Insider's View (2007)

note: Pinned at Montréal, where both kidnappings took place.

story.en:
Through the 1960s the FLQ, a small clandestine group seeking Québec independence through revolution, had planted bombs in mailboxes, armouries and the Montréal Stock Exchange. On 5 October 1970 one cell seized James Cross, the British trade commissioner, from his home; five days later another took Pierre Laporte from his front lawn as he played football with his nephew.

The kidnappers demanded the release of jailed members and the broadcast of their manifesto, which Radio-Canada read on air. As students rallied in sympathy, the Québec and Montréal governments asked Ottawa for help. Asked by a reporter how far he would go, Pierre Trudeau replied with a phrase that became famous: just watch me. On 16 October the War Measures Act suspended civil liberties; soldiers patrolled the streets and police arrested poets, singers and union leaders.

The next day Laporte's body was found in the trunk of a car. In December police found Cross, and his kidnappers were flown to Cuba in exchange for his release. The crisis discredited violence as a path to sovereignty; six years later René Lévesque's Parti Québécois won power at the ballot box.
story.zh:
整个20世纪60年代，谋求通过革命实现魁北克独立的小型秘密组织“魁北克解放阵线”，在邮筒、军械库和蒙特利尔证券交易所安放炸弹。1970年10月5日，该组织的一个小组从英国贸易专员詹姆斯·克罗斯家中将他劫走；五天后，另一个小组在皮埃尔·拉波特与侄子在自家门前草坪踢球时将他绑走。

绑架者要求释放在押成员并播出其宣言，加拿大广播电台照此宣读了宣言。学生们集会表示同情，魁北克省政府和蒙特利尔市政府请求渥太华援助。记者问皮埃尔·特鲁多他会走多远，他的回答成了名言：“等着瞧吧。”10月16日，《战时措施法》暂停了公民自由，士兵在街头巡逻，警察逮捕了诗人、歌手和工会领袖。

次日，拉波特的尸体在一辆汽车的后备箱中被发现。12月警方找到克罗斯，绑架者以释放他为条件被送往古巴。这场危机使暴力作为争取主权的途径声名扫地；六年后，勒内·莱维斯克领导的魁北克人党通过选票赢得了政权。

summary.en: A break-in at the Democratic National Committee offices in Washington's Watergate complex in June 1972 was traced to President Richard Nixon's re-election campaign. Secret White House tapes revealed Nixon's role in the cover-up, and facing impeachment he resigned on 9 August 1974, the only US president to do so.
summary.zh: 1972年6月，华盛顿水门大厦民主党全国委员会办公室遭人闯入，此事被追查到理查德·尼克松总统的连任竞选委员会。白宫秘密录音揭露了尼克松在掩盖真相中的角色，面临弹劾的他于1974年8月9日辞职，成为唯一辞职的美国总统。

sources.title: Richard Nixon Presidential Library: The Watergate Files
Britannica: Watergate scandal
Carl Bernstein & Bob Woodward, All the President's Men (1974)

summary.en: After a referendum in which about 70 percent voted yes, Greenland gained home rule within the Kingdom of Denmark on 1 May 1979, with its own parliament, the Inatsisartut, in Nuuk. Greenland left the European Community in 1985, and the Self-Government Act of 2009 recognised Greenlanders as a people with the right to independence.
summary.zh: 约七成选民在公投中投下赞成票后，格陵兰于1979年5月1日在丹麦王国内实行地方自治，在努克设立自己的议会。格陵兰于1985年退出欧洲共同体；2009年的《自治法》承认格陵兰人是享有独立权的民族。

sources.title: Naalakkersuisut (Government of Greenland): Greenland's self-government
Britannica: Greenland: History
Danish Parliament: Act on Greenland Self-Government (Act no. 473 of 12 June 2009)

story.en:
Denmark had governed Greenland as a closed colony since the 18th century, controlling trade through a royal monopoly. In 1953 the island became a Danish county with seats in the Folketing, and a programme of modernisation followed: Inuit families were moved from scattered hunting settlements into apartment blocks in larger towns, and many children were sent to be schooled in Danish. In 1951 a defence agreement gave the United States the airbase at Thule, and the Inughuit of the area were relocated in 1953.

A generation of young Greenlanders educated in Copenhagen, among them the founders of the Siumut party, demanded control of their own affairs. Home rule arrived in 1979; Greenlandic (Kalaallisut) became the main official language, and Godthåb took back its Greenlandic name, Nuuk.

One of the first decisions of the new government was to leave the European Community over fishing rights, which it did in 1985. Self-government in 2009 transferred control of mineral resources and the police. Greenland's political parties broadly agree on eventual independence; how and when remain debated.
story.zh:
自18世纪起，丹麦就把格陵兰作为封闭殖民地统治，通过王室专营控制贸易。1953年格陵兰成为丹麦的一个郡，在丹麦议会拥有议席，随后推行了一系列现代化计划：因纽特家庭从分散的狩猎聚落迁入大城镇的公寓楼，许多儿童被送去接受丹麦语教育。1951年的一项防务协定把图勒空军基地交给美国，当地的因纽古伊特人于1953年被迫迁走。

在哥本哈根受教育的一代格陵兰青年（其中包括前进党的创始人）要求自主管理本地事务。1979年实行地方自治后，格陵兰语成为主要官方语言，戈特霍布也恢复了格陵兰语名称努克。

新政府最早作出的决定之一，是为了渔业权益退出欧洲共同体，并于1985年正式退出。2009年实行的自治又移交了矿产资源和警务的管辖权。格陵兰各政党大体都赞成最终独立，但如何独立、何时独立仍存争论。

summary.en: René Lévesque's Parti Québécois government asked Quebecers for a mandate to negotiate "sovereignty-association" with Canada. With turnout of 86 percent, 59.6 percent voted No after Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau promised a renewed federalism.
summary.zh: 勒内·莱维斯克领导的魁北克人党政府请求魁北克人授权其与加拿大谈判“主权—联合”。投票率达86%，在皮埃尔·特鲁多总理承诺革新联邦制之后，59.6%的选民投了反对票。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Quebec Referendum (1980)
Élections Québec: Résultats des référendums

summary.en: On 18 May 1980 an earthquake triggered the largest landslide in recorded history on the bulging north face of Mount St. Helens in Washington, unleashing a lateral blast that flattened 600 square kilometres of forest and killed 57 people. Ash fell across eleven states.
summary.zh: 1980年5月18日，一场地震在华盛顿州圣海伦斯火山不断隆起的北坡引发了有记录以来最大的山体滑坡，随即爆发的侧向冲击波摧毁了600平方公里的森林，造成57人死亡。火山灰飘落到十一个州。

sources.title: USGS Cascades Volcano Observatory: 1980 Cataclysmic Eruption
Britannica: Mount Saint Helens

name.en: Patriation of the constitution and the Charter of Rights
name.zh: 宪法回归与《权利与自由宪章》

summary.en: With the Constitution Act, 1982, proclaimed by Queen Elizabeth II on Parliament Hill, Canada gained the power to amend its own constitution and entrenched the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms and the recognition of Aboriginal and treaty rights. Québec's government never signed it.
summary.zh: 随着伊丽莎白二世女王在国会山宣布《1982年宪法法》，加拿大获得了自行修改宪法的权力，并把《加拿大权利与自由宪章》以及对原住民权利和条约权利的承认写入宪法。魁北克省政府始终没有签署。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Patriation of the Constitution
Government of Canada: Constitution Act, 1982
Peter H. Russell, Constitutional Odyssey (3rd ed., 2004)

story.en:
Until 1982 Canada's constitution was a British statute, the British North America Act of 1867, which could only be amended by the Parliament at Westminster, because Ottawa and the provinces had never agreed on a formula to amend it themselves. After the 1980 referendum Pierre Trudeau, who had promised Quebecers change, set out to bring the constitution home and add a bill of rights, even without the provinces if necessary.

Eight provinces, including Québec, opposed him, and the Supreme Court ruled in 1981 that unilateral patriation was legal but broke constitutional convention. At a conference in Ottawa in November, federal and provincial ministers worked out a compromise overnight in a kitchen at the conference centre, adding a "notwithstanding clause" letting legislatures override some Charter rights. René Lévesque, who had gone to bed in Hull across the river, woke to find himself isolated; Québec calls it "la nuit des longs couteaux".

Indigenous organisations lobbied in London and won section 35, recognising existing Aboriginal and treaty rights. On a rainy 17 April 1982 the Queen signed the proclamation on Parliament Hill. The Charter has since transformed Canadian law and public life.
story.zh:
直到1982年，加拿大宪法仍是一部英国法律，即1867年《英属北美法》，只能由威斯敏斯特的议会修改，因为渥太华与各省始终未能就自行修宪的程序达成一致。1980年公投后，曾向魁北克人许诺变革的皮埃尔·特鲁多决心把宪法“迎回”本国并加入权利法案，必要时甚至可以不经各省同意。

包括魁北克在内的八个省反对他。最高法院在1981年裁定，单方面收回宪法虽然合法，却违反宪法惯例。11月在渥太华召开的会议上，联邦和各省部长们在会议中心的一间厨房里连夜拟定妥协方案，加入了允许立法机关推翻部分宪章权利的“尽管条款”。在河对岸赫尔市已经就寝的勒内·莱维斯克一觉醒来，发现自己已被孤立；魁北克称之为“长刀之夜”。

原住民组织赴伦敦游说，争取到了承认现有原住民权利和条约权利的第35条。1982年4月17日，在细雨中，女王在国会山签署了公告。此后，《宪章》深刻改变了加拿大的法律和公共生活。

summary.en: In a second referendum on sovereignty, led by Premier Jacques Parizeau and the charismatic Bloc Québécois leader Lucien Bouchard, Quebecers voted No by 50.58 to 49.42 percent, a margin of about 54,000 votes, with a record turnout of 93.5 percent.
summary.zh: 在由省长雅克·帕里佐和极具魅力的魁北克集团领袖吕西安·布沙尔主导的第二次主权公投中，魁北克人以50.58%对49.42%的结果否决了主权，差距约5.4万票，投票率达创纪录的93.5%。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Quebec Referendum (1995)
Élections Québec: Référendum du 30 octobre 1995
Chantal Hébert & Jean Lapierre, The Morning After: The 1995 Quebec Referendum and the Day That Almost Was (2014)

story.en:
The failure of the Meech Lake Accord in 1990, which would have recognised Québec as a "distinct society", revived the sovereignty movement. Jacques Parizeau's Parti Québécois won the 1994 provincial election and called a vote on whether Québec should become sovereign after offering Canada a new partnership.

The No side led comfortably until Lucien Bouchard, who had survived a flesh-eating infection that cost him a leg, took over the Yes campaign and drew huge, emotional crowds. Polls swung to Yes. Three days before the vote, some 100,000 Canadians from other provinces rallied in downtown Montréal to tell Quebecers they wanted them to stay.

On the night of 30 October the result hung on a few thousand votes for hours. Parizeau, conceding, blamed the defeat on money and the "ethnic vote", remarks that caused an outcry, and resigned the next day. Ottawa responded with the Clarity Act (2000), requiring a clear question and a clear majority for any future secession. Support for sovereignty has not since come close to the 1995 level.
story.zh:
1990年米奇湖协议（本将承认魁北克为“独特社会”）的失败，使主权运动重新兴起。雅克·帕里佐领导的魁北克人党赢得1994年省选，随即发起公投，询问魁北克在向加拿大提出新的伙伴关系之后是否应成为主权国家。

反对方起初遥遥领先，直到吕西安·布沙尔接掌赞成方的竞选。他曾因噬肉菌感染死里逃生、失去一条腿，他的集会人山人海、群情激昂，民调随之转向赞成方。投票前三天，约十万名来自其他省份的加拿大人在蒙特利尔市中心集会，告诉魁北克人他们希望魁北克留下。

10月30日夜，结果在几千票的差距上悬了好几个小时。帕里佐在承认失败时把落败归咎于金钱和“族裔选票”，引发轩然大波，并于次日辞职。渥太华随后制定了《清晰法》（2000年），规定今后任何分离公投都必须有清晰的问题和清晰的多数。此后主权支持率再也没有接近1995年的水平。

summary.en: Under the 1993 Nunavut Land Claims Agreement, the largest Indigenous land claim settlement in Canadian history, the eastern Northwest Territories became the territory of Nunavut ("our land" in Inuktitut) on 1 April 1999, with an Inuit majority and its capital at Iqaluit.
summary.zh: 根据1993年《努纳武特土地权协议》——加拿大历史上规模最大的原住民土地权协议——西北地区东部于1999年4月1日成为努纳武特地区（因纽特语意为“我们的土地”），因纽特人占多数，首府设在伊卡卢伊特。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Nunavut
Nunavut Tunngavik Incorporated: Nunavut Agreement
Government of Nunavut

note: Pinned at the capital, Iqaluit, rather than the territory's centroid.

story.en:
In the 1950s Canada moved many Inuit from camps on the land into permanent settlements, killed sled dogs in some communities, and relocated families from northern Québec to the High Arctic to assert sovereignty, decisions for which the government later apologised. In 1976 the Inuit Tapirisat of Canada proposed a new territory as part of a land claim covering the eastern Arctic.

Negotiations took almost two decades. The 1993 agreement gave Inuit title to about 350,000 square kilometres, including mineral rights to part of it, a share of resource royalties, a capital fund of more than a billion dollars, and a promise of a new territory. Residents of the Northwest Territories had already approved the boundary in a 1992 plebiscite.

On 1 April 1999 the new flag, with its red inuksuk, was raised in Iqaluit, formerly Frobisher Bay. Nunavut's legislature works by consensus without political parties, and Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, traditional knowledge, is written into the government's principles. The territory is the size of western Europe with about 40,000 people.
story.zh:
20世纪50年代，加拿大把许多因纽特人从野外营地迁入永久定居点，在一些社区捕杀雪橇犬，还为宣示主权把魁北克北部的家庭迁往北极高纬地区；政府后来为这些决定道歉。1976年，加拿大因纽特兄弟会在一项涵盖东北极地区的土地权主张中提出设立新地区的设想。

谈判历时近二十年。1993年的协议给予因纽特人约35万平方公里土地的所有权（其中部分包括矿产权）、一部分资源开采权益金、超过十亿加元的资本基金，以及设立新地区的承诺。西北地区居民已在1992年的全民投票中批准了分界线。

1999年4月1日，绘有红色因努克苏克石堆的新旗帜在伊卡卢伊特（旧称弗罗比舍湾）升起。努纳武特议会实行无政党的共识制，因纽特传统知识被写入政府施政原则。这片地区面积与西欧相当，人口约四万。

summary.en: Nineteen al-Qaeda hijackers seized four airliners, crashing two into the World Trade Center in New York, one into the Pentagon and one, after passengers fought back, into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania. Nearly 3,000 people were killed. The United States launched a war in Afghanistan and a global "war on terror".
summary.zh: 19名“基地”组织劫机者劫持四架客机，两架撞向纽约世界贸易中心，一架撞向五角大楼，另一架在乘客反抗后坠毁在宾夕法尼亚州尚克斯维尔附近的田野。近3000人遇难。美国随后发动阿富汗战争和全球“反恐战争”。

label.zh: 波士顿洛根机场：11号和175号航班起飞
纽约世界贸易中心
华盛顿杜勒斯机场：77号航班起飞
阿灵顿五角大楼
纽瓦克机场：93号航班起飞
93号航班坠毁地，尚克斯维尔

sources.title: National Commission on Terrorist Attacks Upon the United States, The 9/11 Commission Report (2004)
9/11 Memorial & Museum
Britannica: September 11 attacks

story.en:
On a clear Tuesday morning, hijackers armed with box cutters took over four transcontinental flights chosen because they carried full fuel loads. At 8:46 American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower of the World Trade Center; at 9:03, as millions watched live on television, United Flight 175 hit the South Tower. At 9:37 American Flight 77 crashed into the Pentagon.

On United Flight 93, delayed on the ground at Newark, passengers and crew learned by phone what had happened in New York. They voted to fight back and stormed the cockpit; the hijackers rolled the plane into the ground near Shanksville at 10:03, short of their likely target in Washington. Within an hour and a half of the first impact both towers had collapsed. Among the 2,977 victims were 343 New York firefighters.

The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights, and Canada's Operation Yellow Ribbon took in more than 200 diverted planes; the town of Gander, Newfoundland, housed some 6,600 stranded passengers. The attacks led to the invasion of Afghanistan in October, a new Department of Homeland Security, and the 2003 invasion of Iraq.
story.zh:
在一个晴朗的星期二早晨，持美工刀的劫机者控制了四架横贯大陆的航班，选择它们是因为满载燃油。8点46分，美国航空11号航班撞上世界贸易中心北塔；9点03分，在数百万人观看电视直播之际，联合航空175号航班撞上南塔。9点37分，美国航空77号航班撞向五角大楼。

在纽瓦克地面延误起飞的联合航空93号航班上，乘客和机组人员通过电话得知了纽约发生的事情。他们投票决定反抗，冲向驾驶舱；10点03分，劫机者让飞机翻滚着撞向尚克斯维尔附近的地面，未能到达他们在华盛顿的可能目标。第一次撞击后不到一个半小时，两座塔楼相继倒塌。2977名遇难者中有343名纽约消防员。

美国联邦航空管理局下令所有航班停飞，加拿大的“黄丝带行动”接纳了两百多架改航的飞机；纽芬兰的甘德镇收留了约6600名滞留旅客。这次袭击导致美国于10月入侵阿富汗、成立国土安全部，并于2003年入侵伊拉克。

summary.en: Katrina made landfall on the Gulf Coast on 29 August 2005. Its storm surge devastated Mississippi's coast and breached the levees and floodwalls of New Orleans, flooding about 80 percent of the city. More than 1,300 people died, and the slow federal response became a national scandal.
summary.zh: 2005年8月29日，卡特里娜飓风在墨西哥湾沿岸登陆。风暴潮摧毁了密西西比州沿海地区，并冲破新奥尔良的堤坝和防洪墙，约80%的城区被淹。1300多人遇难，联邦政府迟缓的救援成为全国丑闻。

sources.title: NOAA National Hurricane Center: Tropical Cyclone Report, Hurricane Katrina (2005)
Britannica: Hurricane Katrina
Douglas Brinkley, The Great Deluge (2006)

note: Death toll estimates range from about 1,200 to over 1,800 depending on how indirect deaths are counted.

story.en:
Much of New Orleans lies below sea level, protected by levees and floodwalls built by the Army Corps of Engineers. As Katrina approached, the mayor ordered the first mandatory evacuation in the city's history, but some 100,000 residents, many of them poor, elderly or without cars, remained.

The storm weakened before landfall, and at first the city seemed to have been spared. Then floodwalls along the 17th Street and London Avenue canals and the Industrial Canal gave way, investigators later found largely because of design and construction flaws. Water rose to rooftops in the Lower Ninth Ward. Thousands sheltered for days in the Superdome and Convention Center with little food, water or sanitation, while television showed people waving from roofs.

The response revealed failures at every level of government, and the images of overwhelmingly Black, poor victims forced a national debate about race and poverty. Hundreds of thousands were scattered to Houston and other cities, and the population of New Orleans fell by more than half; a decade later it had recovered only partly.
story.zh:
新奥尔良大部分地区低于海平面，依靠陆军工程兵团修建的堤坝和防洪墙保护。卡特里娜逼近时，市长下达了该市史上第一次强制疏散令，但仍有约十万居民留下，其中许多是穷人、老人或没有汽车的人。

飓风在登陆前有所减弱，起初该市似乎躲过一劫。随后，第17街运河、伦敦大道运河和工业运河沿岸的防洪墙相继决口；调查人员后来发现，这主要是设计和施工缺陷所致。下九区的洪水漫到了屋顶。数千人在超级穹顶体育馆和会展中心滞留数日，缺少食物、饮水和卫生设施，电视画面上满是在屋顶挥手求救的人。

这次救灾暴露了各级政府的失职，绝大多数受害者是贫穷黑人的画面迫使全国反思种族与贫困问题。数十万人被疏散到休斯敦等城市，新奥尔良人口减少了一半以上；十年后也只恢复了一部分。

name.en: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada
name.zh: 加拿大真相与和解委员会

summary.en: Created under the 2006 Indian Residential Schools Settlement Agreement and chaired by Justice Murray Sinclair, the commission gathered the testimony of survivors across Canada and in 2015 issued 94 Calls to Action, describing the residential school system as cultural genocide.
summary.zh: 根据2006年《印第安人寄宿学校和解协议》设立、由默里·辛克莱法官担任主席的真相与和解委员会，在加拿大各地收集幸存者证词，并于2015年发布94项行动呼吁，称寄宿学校制度构成文化灭绝。

sources.title: National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation: TRC reports
The Canadian Encyclopedia: Truth and Reconciliation Commission

note: Pinned at the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation, University of Manitoba, Winnipeg, which holds the commission's records.

summary.en: Amid the global financial crisis, Senator Barack Obama of Illinois defeated John McCain with 365 electoral votes to become the first African American president of the United States, speaking to a crowd of some 240,000 in Chicago's Grant Park on election night.
summary.zh: 在全球金融危机中，伊利诺伊州参议员巴拉克·奥巴马以365张选举人票击败约翰·麦凯恩，成为美国第一位非裔总统；选举之夜，他在芝加哥格兰特公园向约24万名群众发表讲话。

sources.title: Federal Election Commission: Federal Elections 2008
Britannica: United States presidential election of 2008

name.zh: 霍普角的伊皮尤塔克聚落

summary.en: On the Tikigaq spit at Point Hope, Alaska, people of the Ipiutak culture lived in a settlement of hundreds of semi-subterranean houses and buried their dead with extraordinary ivory carvings, including chains, spirals and masks with jet eyes, some showing contacts with Siberia.
summary.zh: 在阿拉斯加霍普角的提基加克沙嘴上，伊皮尤塔克文化的人们居住在由数百座半地下房屋组成的聚落里，并以非凡的象牙雕刻随葬，包括链条、螺旋纹饰和镶嵌煤玉眼睛的面具，其中一些显示出与西伯利亚的联系。

sources.title: Helge Larsen & Froelich Rainey, Ipiutak and the Arctic Whale Hunting Culture (American Museum of Natural History, 1948)
Britannica: Ipiutak culture
National Park Service: Cape Krusenstern and Ipiutak sites

note: Radiocarbon dates for Ipiutak range roughly from 1 to 800 CE; the number of houses occupied at one time is uncertain.

story.en:
In 1939 the archaeologists Helge Larsen, Froelich Rainey and Louis Giddings found the outlines of more than 600 house pits laid out in rows on the gravel beach ridges of Point Hope, at the far northwestern corner of Alaska. They called it a lost Arctic city. Not all the houses stood at the same time, but Ipiutak was clearly a large and wealthy community.

Its graves held some of the most intricate art ever made in the Arctic: interlocking ivory chains carved from a single tusk, swivels, openwork plaques, animal figures and burial masks with eyes of inlaid jet and ivory. Some motifs resemble Scytho-Siberian art across the Bering Strait, and iron engraving tools suggest trade with Asia.

Unlike the later Thule, the Ipiutak people seem not to have hunted bowhead whales, relying instead on caribou, seals and walrus. Today Point Hope is the Iñupiaq village of Tikigaq, one of the oldest continuously occupied places in North America, whose people still hunt whales from skin boats.
story.zh:
1939年，考古学家黑尔格·拉森、弗勒利克·雷尼和路易斯·吉丁斯在阿拉斯加西北端霍普角的砾石海滩脊上，发现了600多个排列成行的房屋坑遗迹，称之为一座失落的北极城市。这些房屋并非同时存在，但伊皮尤塔克显然是一个庞大而富庶的社群。

其墓葬中出土了北极地区最精巧的艺术品：用整根象牙雕成的环环相扣的链条、转环、镂空饰板、动物雕像，以及镶嵌煤玉和象牙眼睛的丧葬面具。一些纹样与白令海峡对岸的斯基泰—西伯利亚艺术相似，铁质雕刻工具则暗示了与亚洲的贸易。

与后来的图勒人不同，伊皮尤塔克人似乎并不猎捕弓头鲸，而是依靠驯鹿、海豹和海象为生。今天的霍普角是伊努皮亚特人的村庄提基加克，是北美有人连续居住时间最长的地方之一，村民至今仍驾皮船捕鲸。

summary.en: In southwest Georgia, Woodland-period people of the Weeden Island culture built a ceremonial centre with a 17-metre platform mound, burial mounds and a large village, one of the most populous settlements north of Mexico in its time.
summary.zh: 在佐治亚州西南部，伍德兰时期的威登岛文化居民修建了一处仪式中心，有一座17米高的平台土丘、多座墓冢和一个大型村落，是当时墨西哥以北人口最多的聚落之一。

sources.title: New Georgia Encyclopedia: Kolomoki Mounds
Thomas J. Pluckhahn, Kolomoki: Settlement, Ceremony, and Status in the Deep South, A.D. 350 to 750 (2003)

note: Dates follow Pluckhahn's radiocarbon chronology; earlier scholars placed Kolomoki in the Mississippian period.

name.en: Effigy mound builders of the Upper Mississippi
name.zh: 密西西比河上游的象形土丘

summary.en: Late Woodland peoples in present Wisconsin, Iowa and Minnesota shaped thousands of low earthen mounds in the forms of bears, birds, panthers and water spirits, many holding burials. Some 200 survive at Effigy Mounds National Monument above the Mississippi.
summary.zh: 晚伍德兰时期，生活在今威斯康星、艾奥瓦和明尼苏达的人们用泥土堆成数千座熊、鸟、豹和水灵形状的低矮土丘，其中许多内有墓葬。密西西比河畔的象形土丘国家纪念地保存了约200座。

sources.title: National Park Service: Effigy Mounds National Monument
Robert A. Birmingham & Leslie E. Eisenberg, Indian Mounds of Wisconsin (2000)

note: The QID is for the national monument (designated 1949); the mound-building tradition dates c. 700–1100.

summary.en: On a ridge in Adams County, Ohio, a 400-metre earthen effigy of an uncoiling serpent, its head aligned with the summer-solstice sunset, is the largest serpent effigy in the world. Radiocarbon dates suggest it was built or rebuilt by Fort Ancient people around 1070, though an earlier Adena origin is argued.
summary.zh: 在俄亥俄州亚当斯县的一道山脊上，有一条长约400米、蜿蜒舒展的蛇形土丘，蛇头朝向夏至日落方向，是世界上最大的蛇形象形土丘。放射性碳测年表明，它可能由福特安西恩特人在1070年前后修建或重建，但也有学者主张它起源于更早的阿迪纳文化。

sources.title: Ohio History Connection: Serpent Mound
Herrmann et al., "A new multistage construction chronology for the Great Serpent Mound", Journal of Archaeological Science 50 (2014)

note: Dating is contested: Fagan et al. (1996) favoured c. 1070 (Fort Ancient); Herrmann et al. (2014) argued for c. 300 BCE (Adena).

summary.en: On the Etowah River in northwest Georgia, a Mississippian town grew around a 19-metre platform mound. Its elite burials held copper plates embossed with falcon dancers, marble statues of a seated man and woman, and shell gorgets of the Southeastern Ceremonial Complex.
summary.zh: 在佐治亚州西北部的埃托瓦河畔，一座密西西比文化城镇围绕着一座19米高的平台土丘发展起来。其精英墓葬中出土了压印猎鹰舞者图案的铜板、一男一女坐像的大理石雕像，以及属于“东南仪式复合体”的贝壳胸饰。

sources.title: Georgia State Parks: Etowah Indian Mounds State Historic Site
Adam King, Etowah: The Political History of a Chiefdom Capital (2003)

note: Archaeological dates: occupation began c. 1000, the main mound building c. 1250–1375; the 1550 end marks the period around Hernando de Soto's 1540 visit to the Coosa chiefdom.

summary.en: On a bluff above the Black Warrior River in Alabama, Moundville grew into the second-largest Mississippian centre after Cahokia: 29 platform mounds arranged around a 32-hectare plaza, home to a ruling elite and later a necropolis visited by people from the surrounding valley.
summary.zh: 在阿拉巴马州黑勇士河畔的一处陡崖上，芒德维尔发展为仅次于卡霍基亚的第二大密西西比文化中心：29座平台土丘环绕着一个32公顷的广场，这里先是统治精英的居所，后来成为周边河谷居民前来祭拜的墓葬之城。

sources.title: University of Alabama Museums: Moundville Archaeological Park
Vernon James Knight Jr. & Vincas P. Steponaitis (eds.), Archaeology of the Moundville Chiefdom (1998)

summary.en: At a fortified village on the Missouri River in South Dakota, nearly 500 men, women and children of the Initial Coalescent tradition were killed and mutilated in an attack, probably during a time of drought and competition for farmland. It is one of the largest documented massacres in pre-Columbian North America.
summary.zh: 在南达科他州密苏里河畔的一座设防村落，近500名属于“初期融合”传统的男女老幼在一次袭击中被杀并遭肢解，事件很可能发生在干旱和争夺耕地的时期。这是前哥伦布时代北美有记录的规模最大的屠杀之一。

sources.title: P. Willey, Prehistoric Warfare on the Great Plains: Skeletal Analysis of the Crow Creek Massacre Victims (1990)
Larry J. Zimmerman & Richard G. Whitten, "Mass Grave at Crow Creek in South Dakota Reveals How Ancient Indians Fought", Smithsonian 11 (1980)

note: Dated by radiocarbon to roughly 1325 (Willey); Wikidata gives c. 1400.

summary.en: Around 1400 the leaders of Spiro, a Mississippian centre on the Arkansas River in eastern Oklahoma, were buried in a hollow chamber within Craig Mound with thousands of engraved shell cups, copper plates, textiles and pearls traded from the Gulf, the Great Lakes and the Rockies.
summary.zh: 约1400年，俄克拉何马州东部阿肯色河畔密西西比文化中心斯皮罗的首领们被葬入克雷格土丘内的一座空心墓室，随葬有数千件刻纹贝杯、铜板、织物和珍珠，这些物品经由贸易来自墨西哥湾、五大湖和落基山。

sources.title: Oklahoma Historical Society: Spiro Mounds Archaeological Center
F. Kent Reilly & James F. Garber (eds.), Ancient Objects and Sacred Realms (2007)

story.en:
Spiro was not a large town, but for two centuries it was a religious centre and a broker of long-distance trade between the Mississippian world and the Plains. Its rulers were laid in Craig Mound in a hollow chamber that, uniquely, stayed open and dry, preserving feathers, basketry, wooden masks and cloth that rot away almost everywhere else in the Southeast.

That preservation also drew destruction. In 1933 a group of local men leased the site and tunnelled into the mound for artefacts to sell during the Depression. They broke into the chamber, scattered its contents and sold shell cups engraved with winged serpents and dancing warriors to collectors across America and Europe; one dealer reportedly blew up part of the mound with black powder.

Oklahoma passed its first antiquities law in response, and archaeologists from the University of Oklahoma excavated what remained from 1936. Scholars still track Spiro objects through museum collections around the world. The Wichita and Caddo peoples consider themselves descendants of the Spiro community.
story.zh:
斯皮罗并不是大城镇，但在两个世纪里，它一直是宗教中心，也是密西西比文化世界与大平原之间长途贸易的中间人。其统治者被葬在克雷格土丘中的空心墓室里，这座墓室独一无二地保持了开放和干燥，使羽毛、篮编、木面具和布料得以保存，而这些东西在东南部几乎所有其他地方都已腐烂殆尽。

这种保存状况也招来了破坏。1933年，一群当地人租下遗址，在大萧条中挖掘地道寻找文物出售。他们闯入墓室，把其中的物品弄得七零八落，并把刻有带翼蛇和舞蹈武士图案的贝杯卖给美洲和欧洲各地的收藏家；据说一名商人甚至用黑火药炸掉了部分土丘。

俄克拉何马州为此通过了第一部文物保护法，俄克拉何马大学的考古学家从1936年起对残存部分进行了发掘。学者们至今仍在世界各地的博物馆藏品中追寻斯皮罗文物。威奇托人和卡多人认为自己是斯皮罗社群的后裔。

note: The date is approximate: the Great Mortuary burials and deposits are dated by radiocarbon to roughly 1400.

name.en: Ozette village buried by a mudslide
name.zh: 奥泽特村被泥石流掩埋

summary.en: A mudslide on the Pacific coast of Washington's Olympic Peninsula buried several longhouses of the Makah whaling village of Ozette, sealing their contents. Excavated from 1970 with the Makah Nation, it yielded some 55,000 artefacts, including baskets, harpoons and a cedar carving of a whale fin inlaid with otter teeth.
summary.zh: 华盛顿州奥林匹克半岛太平洋沿岸的一场泥石流，掩埋了马卡族捕鲸村落奥泽特的数座长屋，把屋内物品封存了起来。自1970年起与马卡民族合作发掘，共出土约5.5万件文物，包括篮子、鱼叉，以及一件镶嵌海獭牙齿的雪松木鲸鳍雕刻。

sources.title: Makah Cultural and Research Center, Neah Bay
Ruth Kirk, Ozette: Excavating a Makah Whaling Village (2015)

note: The slide is dated by tree rings and stratigraphy to around 1700; some accounts give c. 1750. A link with the 1700 Cascadia earthquake has been proposed but is unproven.
